metadata.title: Down 36% in a month at 48x P/E: Is Marvell a dip or a trap?

content.text:
Investing.com and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Investing.com — Intel's weak forecast set off a broad chip sell-off, and November's data-center permitting panic has kept AI hardware under pressure. NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) has slid 27.1% over the past month. Yet Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL)—the custom silicon and networking specialist wiring together some of the largest AI server clusters—has plunged 36.2% over the past month to $145.36, less than half its 52-week high of $329.73.
Marvell's slide appears less like a growth scare than a dilution story. Management raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to about $12 billion, and analysts forecast 47.0% revenue growth and 42.7% EPS growth this fiscal year, yet the $115 billion all-stock bid for Lumentum would hand Lumentum holders about 33% of the combined company. At 48.3 times trailing earnings, the stock still prices that growth at a premium—before a single new share has been issued.
Catching when a near-50x multiple and lumpy custom chip orders leave a stock exposed to a 36% drawdown is what ProPicks AI is built for. In Tech Titans, InvestingPro's strategy dedicated to high-margin tech leaders, Marvell is passed over in favor of lower-multiple semiconductor plays—including a process-control equipment leader chipmakers rely on to catch defects, a radio-frequency chip specialist, and a contract chipmaker built around specialty processes.
Marvell makes its money designing the custom AI accelerators, optical DSPs, and switching chips that hyperscalers use to tie their data centers together, and that design work creates high switching costs once a chip is in production. In August, Google signed a commercial agreement covering up to $120 billion in sales through fiscal 2033, along with the right to buy a $12.2 billion stake. Management expects the largest revenue impact in fiscal 2029 and beyond.
Second-quarter fiscal 2027 results confirmed that AI demand is still accelerating. Revenue climbed 37% year-over-year and 13% sequentially to a record $2.74 billion, and non-GAAP EPS of $0.94 edged past the $0.93 estimate. Data center revenue surged 46% to $2.17 billion—79% of total sales—and management guided third-quarter revenue to $3.15 billion. It then lifted its fiscal 2028 outlook to about $18 billion from $16.5 billion, with data center revenue now expected to grow about 60% in fiscal 2027 and more than 60% in fiscal 2028.
Fair Value Tempts Dip-Buyers, but the Risks Stack Up
Wall Street remains largely bullish, but the Lumentum deal split the room. StoneX, UBS and Raymond James held Buy-or-better ratings with targets of $295 to $375. TD Cowen downgraded the stock to Hold and cut its target to $175 from $350, citing equity dilution and deal execution risk. The median analyst price target stands at $310.32, with targets ranging from $175 to $450.
The earnings trend still favors the bulls, with 27 upward EPS revisions against one downward over the past 90 days. InvestingPro's Fair Value models also flag Marvell as undervalued, placing intrinsic value at $180.10 per share—23.9% above the current price and an upside that will tempt dip-buyers.
The main risk is that dip-buyers are taking on several bets at once. The Lumentum deal needs stockholder and regulatory approval before a targeted close in the first half of 2028. Custom silicon ramps have pushed non-GAAP gross margin guidance down to 57.5% to 58.5%, a range management expects to persist into fiscal 2028, while the top 10 customers account for about 82% of revenue and a single distributor for about 37%. Communications and other revenue slipped 3% sequentially to $568 million, with a further low-to-mid-teens decline guided for the third quarter.
Before buying a 36% chip rout, investors must weigh Marvell's custom silicon franchise against Lumentum dilution and margin pressure. Hyperscaler custom ASIC concentration, optical networking margins, and carrier-segment recovery timelines are detailed inside the Marvell Technology Pro Research Report.
Hyperscalers want Marvell's custom silicon badly enough to sign multi-year commitments. What investors cannot yet price is how much of the growth from those commitments each share will keep once the Lumentum deal closes and custom chip ramps stop weighing on gross margins.
Relying on a single custom AI chipmaker while hyperscaler capex headlines keep shifting leaves capital exposed to violent drawdowns and deal dilution. Rather than attempting to catch a falling chip stock manually, InvestingPro's data-driven strategies evaluate thousands of balance sheets every month to isolate companies capturing semiconductor cash flows without extreme single-stock drawdowns.

Disclosure:The author holds no position in the stocks mentioned. Data and financial metrics as of November 13, 2026; share price, monthly performance, P/E, growth forecasts and Fair Value as of November 17, 2026.
